notes: The AD5206 was not in the catalogue, so a new part type digipot-ad5206 was created. Port names are the datasheet pin names (A1..A6, W1..W6, B1..B6, GND, CS, VDD, SDI, CLK, VSS). 'Through' pairs model each channel's resistor track (A-B, A-W, W-B).
The 24-pin DIP straddles the breadboard centre gap. Pins 1-12 go in 9t..20t on row e, and pins 13-24 go in 20b..9b on row f, so pin 13 sits opposite pin 12.

The Fritzing image was not available, so exact hole positions are assumed. The connections follow the tutorial text: all A pins and VDD to +5V; all B pins, GND and VSS to ground; CS to pin 10, SDI to pin 11 and CLK to pin 13; each W pin through a 220 ohm resistor and an LED (anode on the resistor side) to ground.
The top and bottom power rails are linked by jumpers (wire3 and wire4). The Arduino 5V and GND.1 feed the top rails.
Pin numbering note: the datasheet mapping is pin 17 = W1, pin 20 = W2, pin 14 = W3, pin 23 = W4, pin 11 = W5, pin 2 = W6.
VSS is tied to ground, as the tutorial's 0 V operation implies.
